Look, I know a lot of people love their Linux but honestly, try BSD if you run a server.

My take-away: Linux is chaotic-good and BSD is lawful-good, mostly coming from their development history as personal-project grown big without much centralized coordination and in-house development with strong, centralized management.

Good read! To be honest I think open-source / free software naturally leans more towards the chaotic model.

Messing around with getting a GUI up and running from scratch (net install) in OpenBSD and FreeBSD earlier this year was a great way to learn about the basic differences. Can pretty easily get MATE, KDE, or LXDE up and running with full codec support, all of the applications I would need to use on a daily basis, and no WiFi issues whatsoever (wpa_supplicant is from BSD anyway). For something that is supposed to be geared more towards servers, it is really is quite usable as a desktop. The only real hitch for me that there are not a lot of graphical login managers (even Ghost BSD uses GDM for a MATE desktop) which is no issue to me but one bad .xinitrc edit can cause issues, and the desktop software packages are behind. Mate 1.8 and KDE 4.14 are still supremely modern and usable, but I'm always rolling with bleeding edge stuff like Manjaro/Arch or KDE Neon in Linux. But the best thing in the long is that if Devuan does not take off, and systemd gets worse, I have a great escape chute that I can set up in a matter of thirty minutes.
